dropped.averaged_npairs_dqags: cost; the weights question is answered under the operator. Running the adaptive quadrature at ~1000 fine-grid nodes costs ~4x the operator per draw, and this variant would have bought only a second reading of the uniform-vs-npairs contrast that averaged_uniform_fixedop and averaged_npairs_fixedop already give at a quarter the price. Dropped by Cail 2026-09-04. Nothing structural prevents it: add it back to VARIANTS and it runs.

pointwise_dqags.name: pointwise_dqags
pointwise_dqags.label: dqags, pointwise
pointwise_dqags.note: The published paper (archive_v2): adaptive QUADPACK at the 20 reporting abscissae, limits from the reporting grid.

averaged_uniform_dqags.name: averaged_uniform_dqags
averaged_uniform_dqags.label: dqags, averaged (uniform)
averaged_uniform_dqags.note: The cross term, and the reason the scan exists. With averaged_uniform_fixedop it isolates the quadrature effect at fixed geometry; with pointwise_dqags it isolates the geometry effect at fixed quadrature. Those two contrasts are what the default method->geometry mapping confounds.

pointwise_fixedop.name: pointwise_fixedop
pointwise_fixedop.label: operator, pointwise (nearest node)
pointwise_fixedop.note: The fourth corner, reachable only by approximation. The single-grid operator evaluates at nodes, so each of the 20 reporting abscissae is snapped to the nearest fine node in log theta -- a shift of up to 0.32%, recorded per point in snap_offsets and carried into the mode provenance. Completes the method x geometry square, so the quadrature and geometry effects can each be read along two edges rather than one. Read it alongside its offsets: the snap moves theta by the same order as the small-theta structure being measured.

pointwise_fixedop_reporting.name: pointwise_fixedop_reporting
pointwise_fixedop_reporting.label: operator, pointwise (reporting local term)
pointwise_fixedop_reporting.note: The hybrid, and the corner pointwise_fixedop should have been. The pure-mode transform is a local term plus an integral term; pointwise_dqags takes the local term from the 20-bin reporting measurement and only the integral from the fine grid, while pointwise_fixedop -- forced to evaluate at a node -- takes BOTH from the snapped fine node, so its local term carries the shot noise of ~1/50 of a reporting bin's pairs. This variant snaps exactly as pointwise_fixedop does for the integral term (same nearest-node choice, same recorded offsets) but restores the reporting-grid local term. It is therefore the like-for-like operator counterpart of the published pointwise chain: the difference from pointwise_dqags is quadrature (plus the snapped integral's theta shift), not fine-bin noise.

averaged_uniform_fixedop.name: averaged_uniform_fixedop
averaged_uniform_fixedop.label: operator, averaged (uniform)
averaged_uniform_fixedop.note: ADOPTED (baseline): the fixed-quadrature linear operator, pure modes averaged into the reporting bins with equal weight.

averaged_uniform_fixedop_reporting.data_pte_note: covariance borrowed from averaged_uniform_fixedop (identical to round-off); the data vector is this variant's own, rebuilt in-stage from the measured xi and checked against averaged_uniform_fixedop's stored vector.
averaged_uniform_fixedop_reporting.name: averaged_uniform_fixedop_reporting
averaged_uniform_fixedop_reporting.label: operator, averaged (uniform), reporting local term
averaged_uniform_fixedop_reporting.note: The averaged geometry's counterpart of pointwise_fixedop_reporting, and the fourth reading of the local-term axis. Integral term exactly averaged_uniform_fixedop's -- the operator at every fine node carrying the bin's support, uniformly averaged -- but the local 0.5*(xi_p +/- xi_m) term is the 20-bin reporting measurement rather than the uniform mean of the fine xi over the bin. Those two differ because the reporting xi is its own TreeCorr measurement (pair weighted within the bin), not a rebinning of the fine one. Note the MC covariance chains construct their reporting draws BY uniformly rebinning the fine draws, so there the two local terms coincide by construction and this variant's covariance matches averaged_uniform_fixedop's; the difference lives in the data and mock DATA VECTORS. That is why covariance_from aliases it rather than rebuilding: propagating 500 draws through a transform that provably returns the same covariance is a fake dependency (Cail, 2026-09-06). Measured: substituting the reporting local term on a uniformly-rebinned draw moves the modes by 1.4e-20, against 1.8e-06 on the real reporting measurement. The cost is that the borrowed bundle carries the DONOR's data vector, so this variant has no data PTE; its signal is the mock <xi^B> shift, which comes from mock_pure_eb_modes_scan and is unaffected.

averaged_npairs_fixedop.name: averaged_npairs_fixedop
averaged_npairs_fixedop.label: operator, averaged (npairs)
averaged_npairs_fixedop.note: The ruled arm (fixed_operator universe): the same operator and window, averaged with TreeCorr pair counts (Asgari et al. 2019, Appendix A).
